content.text:
I've submitted index 1 (Ca 0.14, Fe 0.70, Mn 0.16) as the best composition, but this campaign almost certainly didn't find a good photoanode. All three photocurrent measurements I was allowed were essentially zero:

| Index | Region | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fe-rich, hematite-like, with some Mn | 1e-8 |
| 73 | Equal parts Ca, Fe and Mn | -1e-8 |
| 74 | Ca-rich, near the Ca₂Fe₂O₅ structure | 0 |

Index 1 is the highest, but only just. Differences this small are within measurement noise, so the three points can't be meaningfully ranked.

**What I skipped:**
- **XRD:** I used none of the 5 XRD measurements, so I never confirmed which crystal phases actually formed.
- **Phase list:** the list of known phases was too long to read in full, and I didn't go back through it.
- **Mn-rich region:** I never measured this corner, so it's still unexplored.

With only 3 photocurrent measurements, I sampled three spread-out regions based on general chemistry rather than on data. All three came up flat, so the library's real best composition, if it has any meaningful photocurrent, is probably somewhere I didn't measure.
